rationale: The base station is online locally (uplink_status ok, all 7 devices online, local app session and live view work), but E-503 "cloud reporting failed repeatedly" is active and events never reach the cloud, so remote notifications stop. The customer already rebooted the mesh nodes, disabled firewall features, and power-cycled the base station with DNS set to automatic, yet E-503 persists — matching the KB escalation criteria for a cloud-channel/certificate issue rather than a local network problem.

output.symptom_summary: Remote notifications stopped; cameras work locally. Base station shows E-503 'cloud reporting failed repeatedly' and events do not reach the cloud.
output.suspected_root_cause: Persistent cloud channel or certificate issue on the base station, not a local network problem.
key_abnormal_indicators: local app session and live view work
E-503 persists after reboot of mesh nodes, disabling firewall, power-cycle of base station, DNS automatic
output.customer_reply: Thank you for your patience. We've identified that your base station is having trouble communicating with our cloud service, which is why remote notifications have stopped. I've escalated your case to our engineering team for further investigation. They will follow up with you shortly. No further action is needed from you at this time.

args.query: E-503 uplink blocked events not reaching cloud

args.question: Is the base station connected to the network via Ethernet cable or Wi-Fi? And does the base station's LED show a solid/steady color (normal) or is it blinking/red?

args.action: Power-cycle the base station: unplug its power for 30 seconds, then plug it back in and wait 2 minutes. Also, in the mesh router app, confirm the DNS setting is set to "Automatic" (not a custom/manual DNS). Then check whether remote notifications resume.

args.query: E-503 uplink blocked events not reaching cloud

results.text: Base station online, live view works on local network, but no event notifications; E-503 every few minutes. Router restart and DNS reset did not help. Escalated; expired device certificate on backend. Escalated correctly.

The base station could not deliver events to the cloud. Frontline action: verify internet access, restart router and base station, set router DNS to automatic. If E-503 persists after these steps while the base station is online, escalate to FAE (cloud channel or certificate issue).

The base station connects to the home router by Ethernet (recommended) or 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi. If all cameras and sensors show offline in the app at the same time, first check whether the base station itself is online. Power-cycle the router, wait 2 minutes, then power-cycle the base station. The base station requires outbound TCP 443 and 8883 to the cloud.
